Reduced distribution system costs are cited in industry studies as a major reason for preferring DLC-like active management of EV charging at lower participation shares (The AES Corporation and Camus 2024; EnergyHub, Inc. 2024). We also do not include load or managed charging for medium- and heavy-duty EVs. Regarding costs, we do not estimate the absolute or relative costs of enabling EVMC through TOU, RTP, or DLC mechanisms. This study also analyzes different dispatch mechanisms in isolation, but it could be that, especially after enablement costs and EV owner preferences are accounted for, a mix of dispatch mechanisms would provide more value for lower cost and with higher overall participation. Finally, we chose a specific strategy, applying a $1 per MW/h ramping penalty in the price- responsive dispatch algorithm to penalize changing charging power across equally priced TOU periods, to mitigate TOU rebound effects. We heuristically discounted the megawatt-scale power and energy bounds of aggregated DLC to reduce expected dispatch error rates to below 5%. In both cases, other mitigation approaches might perform as well or better or be easier to implement in practice. 19 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications.
